title: Chef's Salad
subtitle: Diner-style main course salad with ham, chicken, egg and cheese
excerpt: A classic American diner main salad: ribbons of ham and poached chicken breast, wedges of hard-boiled egg, sliced emmental, tomato and cucumber over cos lettuce, dressed with a simple vinaigrette.
sourceNotes: The chef's salad is documented in American restaurant culture from the 1940s, popularised by Louis Diat of the Ritz-Carlton in New York, who credited it to a French original. By the 1960s it was a fixture on American diner and hotel menus. The exact ingredients vary by region and by what is in the kitchen, making it inherently adaptable.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: All components can be prepared up to a day ahead and stored separately in the fridge. Dress just before serving.

content.text: Chef's salad is the American diner's main-course answer to a fridge drawer. Shredded lettuce, cold cuts cut into ribbons, sliced cheese, hard-boiled egg, tomato and cucumber, dressed and served as a full meal. The ingredients are flexible; what matters is the presentation and the volume.

items.prepNote: cooked and cut into thin strips

content.text: The choice of cheese and cold cuts is open. Emmental, Gruyere, cheddar, and Swiss all work. Ham, turkey, roast beef, and salami all have a place. Use what is in the fridge.
Lower {{eggs}} eggs into boiling water. Cook for 10 minutes for fully set yolks. Transfer to cold water. Peel and quarter when cool.

Whisk {{red-wine-vinegar}} of red wine vinegar with {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Add {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a slow stream, whisking to combine. Taste and adjust.

Divide the cos over four plates or into a large bowl. Arrange the ham and turkey ribbons, egg quarters, emmental strips, tomato wedges, cucumber slices and red onion over the lettuce. Pour the dressing over and serve immediately, or serve the dressing alongside.

items.symptom: Cold cuts curl and look unappealing
items.cause: Refrigerated too long after slicing, drying out at the edges.
items.fix: Slice cold cuts and cheese on the day, keep covered in the fridge until ready to assemble.

items.cause: Red wine vinegar varies in acidity.
items.fix: Taste the dressing before pouring. Add a pinch of sugar or a little more oil to balance.

content.text: Chef's salad belongs in the category of fridge-clearance cooking done with a little care. The format, big lettuce base, cold protein in ribbons, hard egg, and cheese, became a diner institution precisely because it was practical: lunch made from what was already cooked. The vinaigrette is what separates a good version from a careless one.
